page: Vultr vcg-a40-6c-30g-12vram is a virtual machine within the Cloud GPU family, featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor. The instance is configured with 6 shared vCPUs and 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 5.0 GB of RAM per core. For storage, the server includes 550 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. It also comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The defining feature of this instance is its fractional GPU allocation, providing 0.25 of an NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 12 GB of dedicated VRAM. This fractional setup allows users to access GPU acceleration without provisioning a full physical card. However, the shared CPU allocation and fractional GPU resources represent a performance tradeoff, meaning the instance is not intended for sustained maximum-throughput compute workloads that require dedicated physical hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the fractional GPU and shared CPU model offers a lower-cost entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration but not the full capacity of an A40 card. This resource density makes it suitable for development environments, small-scale machine learning inference, lightweight graphics rendering, and data processing tasks that benefit from CUDA acceleration without requiring massive parallel compute budgets.
